links.outcome: LLM triage preference differences under counterfactual variation of patient sex and race
links.effect: LLMs showed sex-based differences that were more pronounced in certain racial groups, indicating intersectional bias. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: LLMs exhibit sex-based differences, and they are more pronounced in certain racial groups, suggesting that LLMs encode preferences that emerge in specific clinical contexts and combinations of characteristics.

links.outcome: Robustness of LLM versus conventional ML triage under distribution shift and missing data
links.effect: LLMs were more robust than traditional ML to distribution shifts and missing data. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: First, we demonstrate that LLMs exhibit superior robustness compared to traditional ML, which is promising due to their ability to provide explanatory rationales.

unlisted_practices: Retrieval of similar prior patient cases as in-context examples for LLM triage
Continued pre-training of LLMs for triage

screen.reason: The study conducts an empirical benchmark/audit evaluating large language models for emergency department triage, assessing robustness to distribution shifts and intersectional biases across sex and race via counterfactual analysis.
